references.text: The same introductory formula where the Lord speaks to Moses, used repeatedly in the books of Moses to introduce divine commands.
The opening formula in Leviticus where the Lord calls out to Moses and speaks to him, a parallel introduction to divine revelation.
Identical wording where the Lord speaks to Moses to give new instructions regarding sacrifices.
The same standard formula that introduces a new paragraph of divine regulations given to Moses.
The preceding chapter begins with the same formula, showing the continuity of God's revelation to Moses.
The Lord speaks to Moses in the tent of meeting, the same pattern for divine communication.
Repeated use of the formula 'the Lord spoke to Moses and said' as an introduction to legislation.
